corrections.issue: The point that freely available quantitative data cannot produce outperformance is relayed by Marks as his son Andrew Marks's argument (from their pandemic debates); the claim does not say so.
corrections.fix: Marks, relaying his son Andrew's argument, says readily available quantitative data cannot create outperformance because everyone has it; an edge needs superior interpretation or qualitative / forward-looking information that is not readily available.

corrections.issue: Marks names hedge funds and private equity as what institutions tried; 'credit alternatives' is not stated.
corrections.fix: After the 2000-02 S&P decline (first three-year fall since 1939) and Fed cuts to very low rates, investors fell out of love with stocks and bonds and turned to hedge funds and then private equity, giving birth to 'alternative investing' around 2004-06.
